replacement_spec.body:
A sensitivity is a statistical metric that quantifies a diagnostic test or classifier's ability to correctly identify actual positive cases. Parameters: (1) a defined ground truth partitioning cases into positive and negative; (2) a classification rule or score that assigns each case to a predicted class; (3) a threshold (implicit or explicit) separating positive from negative predictions. Computed as true positives divided by the sum of true positives and false negatives (TP over TP plus FN), also called the true positive rate or recall. Persistence mechanism: mathematical formalization in statistical theory and diagnostic evaluation, codified through peer-reviewed methodology in epidemiology, clinical diagnostics, and machine learning, maintained through standard formulas in textbooks and software libraries.
e.g.: the sensitivity of the D-Quicker test for major depression; the sensitivity of a mammogram for detecting breast cancer; the sensitivity of a rapid strep test for Group A Streptococcus; the sensitivity of a blood glucose monitor at hypoglycemic thresholds | not: precision (the proportion of positive predictions that are correct); specificity (the proportion of actual negatives correctly identified); sensitivity plot (a visualization of model output versus input parameter changes)

replacement_spec.body:
A frequency-response is the characterization of how a system's output magnitude and phase vary as a function of sinusoidal input frequency. Parameters: the independent variable is frequency (typically spanning DC to the system's bandwidth); the dependent variables are gain (output/input magnitude ratio, often in dB) and phase shift (output phase relative to input, in degrees or radians). replacement_spec.body: The constant-Q transform decomposes a signal into frequency bins whose bandwidth is proportional to center frequency, yielding a log-frequency time-frequency representation with constant quality factor Q. The analysis window length increases inversely with frequency: narrow bandwidth at low frequencies, wide at high. Parameters: number of octaves, bins per octave, reference frequency, quality factor Q. It persists as a spectrogram-like representation where frequency resolution follows a logarithmic scale, naturally suited to musical and spectral analysis where perceptual frequency resolution is logarithmic. e.g.: the constant-Q decomposition in Essentia music analysis library; the CQT-based feature extraction in librosa for music information retrieval; the log-frequency spectrogram in the CQT toolbox for audio analysis | not: spectrogram (linear frequency bins, not log-frequency); mel-spectrogram (Mel-scale bins, not constant-Q) [formal: transformatio constantis-Q | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes]
